Canada's unemployment rate was **6.5% in September 2026**. That is 0.6 percentage points lower than the **7.1% in September 2025**.

These figures are seasonally adjusted and cover ages 15 and over. The source is Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0287-01 (Labour force characteristics, monthly, seasonally adjusted), vector v2062815.

The rate rose slightly from 6.4% in August 2026.

**Newfoundland and Labrador** had the highest unemployment rate in September 2026, at **9.1%** (seasonally adjusted, ages 15 and over). The Canada-wide rate was 6.5%.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0287-01, "Labour force characteristics, monthly, seasonally adjusted and trend-cycle". The Newfoundland and Labrador series is v2063004 and the Canada series is v2062815. The reference period is September 2026.

The next highest were New Brunswick at 7.4% (v2063571) and Prince Edward Island at 7.3% (v2063193).

Canada's population on July 1, 2026 was **41,798,407**.

That is **189,425 people (+0.46%)** more than on July 1, 2025, when it was 41,608,982.

The figures come from Statistics Canada Table 17-10-0009-01, "Population estimates, quarterly", vector v1 (Canada). The reference periods are Q3 2026 (July 1, 2026) and Q3 2025 (July 1, 2025). The data were released 2026-09-23. Estimates in this table are revised from time to time, so the figures could change in later releases.

Alberta grew faster, at about 1.52% against about 0.28% for Ontario in the year to July 1, 2026.

| Province | July 1, 2025 | July 1, 2026 | Change | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alberta (v15) | 5,024,631 | 5,101,050 | +76,419 | **1.52%** |
| Ontario (v12) | 16,216,961 | 16,262,121 | +45,160 | **0.28%** |

Ontario's population fell slightly in the two quarters after Oct 1, 2025 (16,253,023), then edged up in the quarter to July 1, 2026. Alberta rose in every quarter.

I calculated the growth rates from the table's population counts. Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01, "Population estimates, quarterly", reference dates 2025-07-01 and 2026-07-01 (released 2026-09-23).

On July 1, 2026, Canada had **2,779,774 non-permanent residents**. A year earlier, on July 1, 2025, it had 2,934,388. That is a drop of 154,614 people, or about 5.3%.

The 2026 figure is also below the quarterly peak of 2,984,285 on October 1, 2024. It has fallen in each of the last four quarters, from 2,942,949 on October 1, 2025 to 2,863,151, then 2,798,649, then 2,779,774.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0121-01, "Estimates of the number of non-permanent residents by type, quarterly". The series is Canada, Total, non-permanent residents (v1566927590), released 2026-09-23. The figures may be revised in later releases.

Canada's inflation rate for 2025 as a whole was **about 2.1%**. That is the rise in the annual average all-items Consumer Price Index (CPI) from 2024 to 2025. It is my calculation from the index values below, not a rate published in the table.

- 2024 average CPI: 160.9
- 2025 average CPI: 164.2
- Change: 164.2 / 160.9 − 1 = 2.05%, which rounds to 2.1% (to one decimal place)

For comparison, the same calculation gives 2.4% for 2024, using the 2023 average of 157.1.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0005-01, "Consumer Price Index, annual average, not seasonally adjusted", Canada, all-items, vector v41693271, reference years 2024 and 2025.

In September 2026, the year-over-year changes were:

- **CPI-trim:** 1.8% (August 2026: 1.9%)
- **CPI-median:** 1.9% (August 2026: 2.0%)

Both measures eased by 0.1 percentage point from August.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0256-01, "Consumer Price Index (CPI) statistics, measures of core inflation and other related statistics - Bank of Canada definitions" (Canada, year-over-year percent change). CPI-trim is vector v108785715. CPI-median is vector v108785714.

Canada's real GDP was essentially flat in August 2026. It edged down by about 0.01% from July, a drop of roughly $153 million at annual rates. The rounded change is 0.0%.

- July 2026: $2,371,788 million (chained 2017 dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates)
- August 2026: $2,371,635 million

I calculated the change from the two published levels. I did not check Statistics Canada's own headline percentage, which may differ slightly.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 36-10-0434-01, "Gross domestic product (GDP) at basic prices, by industry, monthly" (vector v65201210, All industries, Canada). The reference period is August 2026, and the table was released on 2026-10-30.

Canada had a merchandise trade surplus of about **$5.6 billion** in August 2026 (customs basis, seasonally adjusted). The surplus is my calculation from exports minus imports in the table below.

Source: Statistics Canada Table 12-10-0163-01, "International merchandise trade by commodity, monthly", total of all merchandise, Canada.

| Series (August 2026) | Vector | $ millions |
|---|---|---|
| Exports, seasonally adjusted | v1566911035 | 77,090.8 |
| Imports, seasonally adjusted | v1566910429 | 71,469.1 |
| **Balance, seasonally adjusted** | | **+5,621.7** |

- **July 2026:** the seasonally adjusted surplus was about $1,233 million (exports 73,761.3, imports 72,527.9).
- **Unadjusted:** the August surplus was about $2,089 million. Exports (v1566910885) were 73,826.3 and imports (v1566910279) were 71,736.9.
- **Basis:** I used the customs basis. The table also has a balance-of-payments basis, which I did not pull, so its figure may differ.

- **Unadjusted: $1,355.29**, up from $1,305.42 in August 2025. That is **+$49.87, or +3.8%**.

About **1.26 million** Canadians (≈1,255,000) would be unemployed if you apply the September 2026 unemployment rate to the 2021 Census labour force.

- **2021 Census labour force:** 19,310,340 people in the labour force in Canada. Source: Table 98-10-0400-01, "Labour force status by highest level of education…", Canada, all ages, genders and education levels, 2021. The census table has no vector ID (the API returned 0).
- **September 2026 unemployment rate:** 6.5%, seasonally adjusted, ages 15+. Source: Table 14-10-0287-01 (Labour Force Survey), vector v2062815, reference period 2026-09.
- **Calculation:** 19,310,340 × 0.065 ≈ 1,255,172.

This is an illustrative estimate, not a published count. It mixes a 2021 labour force with a 2026 rate, and the labour force has changed since 2021. The Labour Force Survey publishes its own count of unemployed people.
